title: Candidate finding
description: findings/<finding_id>/finding.json — written by the orchestrator from hunter output, updated with skeptic's verdict. The escalate/verify/triage files are separate so each stage's verdict is independently checkable by a hook.

operation_ids.description: operations.json ids this finding touches. Keeps coverage and findings joined.

stage.description: Where the finding is in the chain. 'parked' means it exhausted its single retry and is waiting on the user.

retry_count.description: Times triager sent this back to escalator. Hard cap 1 — a second non-PASS parks it.

flow.description: Entry point to sink, with file:line at each step.

hypothesis.description: The specific concrete attack: what input, what validation is missing or bypassable, what impact.

prowler.description: Set instead of `hunter` when the candidate came from the follow-up phase rather than the linear pass. Same content contract as `hunter` — a candidate is a candidate — plus a pointer back to the anomaly it grew from, so a kill can be traced to its origin and not re-pursued forever.

source_anomaly_id.description: The anomalies.json id this came from. Findings carrying this are excluded from prowler's own input set by default — otherwise it re-litigates its own kills every run.

six_source_check.description: All six recorded, including explicit 'checked, nothing found'. This is what stops a later session re-litigating a dead end.

github_issues.description: Source 1: the target's own public issue tracker / PR history. Key name is historical; any public tracker counts. Use 'not_applicable: <reason>' where the target has none.

evidence.description: Shared evidence shape. Every artifact traces to a real tool execution in this run; anything that cannot be traced is dropped, never softened.

path.description: Relative to the run dir, under evidence/<finding_id>/.

produced_by.description: The exact tool invocation that produced it, e.g. "Bash: curl -s -u attacker:... http://localhost:9200/_x". Not a paraphrase.
